Option_C: Transferring academic credits earned by a student from one institution to another
Option_D: A national funding agency to enable teacher training institutions to organise their programmes effectively and efficiently
Brief_Explanation: The Academic Bank of Credit is essentially a digital repository to securely store the academic credits earned by students from various higher education institutions to facilitate mobility.

Question_Text: Which one of the following is a recommendation of the National Education Policy, 2020 ?
Option_A: By 2030, all teachers shall be trained in institutions approved by the Central Government.
Option_B: By 2030, all those teaching senior secondary classes should have M.Ed. qualification.
Option_C: By 2030, all teacher education will be in multidisciplinary institutions.
Option_D: By 2030, all B.Ed. programmes will be of 2 years.
Brief_Explanation: NEP 2020 aims to move all teacher preparation into multidisciplinary higher education institutions by 2030, phasing out standalone teacher education institutions.

Question_Text: Which of the following are proposed/recommended by the National Education Policy, 2020 ? 1. The medium of instruction until Grade 8 will be the official language of the State/UT in which the children attend the school. 2. In secondary schools, the students will be given increased flexibility and choice of subjects to study. 3. In addition to English, some other foreign languages will also be offered for study at secondary level. Select the correct answer using the code given below :
Brief_Explanation: Statement 1 is incorrect because NEP emphasizes mother tongue or local language, not necessarily the State's official language. Statements 2 and 3 are correct proposals.

Question_Text: By which year are all primary schools going to achieve universal foundational literacy and numeracy as the highest priority of the education system according to the National Education Policy, 2020 ?
Brief_Explanation: NEP 2020 establishes the achievement of universal foundational literacy and numeracy in primary schools by 2025 as an urgent national mission.

Question_Text: With reference to the Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act, 2009, consider the following statements : 1. It is the duty of every parent or guardian to admit his or her child or ward to an elementary education in a neighbourhood school. 2. Proof of age of the child is essential at the time of admission to an elementary education in a neighbourhood school. 3. The teachers shall not engage themselves in private teaching activity. Which of the statements given above is/are correct ?
Brief_Explanation: Statement 2 is incorrect as Section 14 of the RTE Act explicitly states that no child shall be denied admission for lack of age proof. Statements 1 and 3 are true under the Act.

Question_Text: As per the National Education Policy, 2020, the planning and implementation of 'Early Childhood Care and Education' curriculum will be carried out by
Option_B: Union Ministry of Education and Union Ministry of Women and Child Development (WCD) only
Option_C: Union Ministry of Education, WCD and Union Ministry of Health and Family Welfare (HFW) only
Option_D: Union Ministry of Education, WCD, HFW and Union Ministry of Tribal Affairs
Brief_Explanation: NEP 2020 mandates that the implementation of ECCE will be a joint effort across the Ministries of HRD (now Education), Women and Child Development (WCD), Health and Family Welfare (HFW), and Tribal Affairs.

Question_Text: Consider the following statements : 1. A test cannot be valid unless it is reliable. 2. A test that has some validity for one purpose is always valid for another purpose. 3. A reliable test may not necessarily be valid. Select the correct answer using the code given below :
Brief_Explanation: Reliability is a prerequisite for validity, meaning a test must be consistent to be accurate (St 1 is true). However, a test can be highly consistent (reliable) while measuring the wrong construct entirely (St 3 is true). Validity is specific to context (St 2 is false).

Question_Text: Formative assessment is conducted to 1. monitor student learning 2. provide ongoing feedback 3. improve teaching-learning process 4. know the position of a student in the group Select the correct answer using the code given below :
Brief_Explanation: Formative assessment focuses on continuous improvement, feedback, and monitoring learning. It is not designed for summative ranking or comparing a student's position in a group.

Question_Text: With reference to the United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child, consider the following statements : 1. A child is any person below the age of 16. 2. Children can choose their own opinions and religion. 3. Every child has the right to privacy. Which of the statements given above are correct ?
Brief_Explanation: Statement 1 is incorrect because the UNCRC defines a child as any human being below the age of 18. Statements 2 and 3 correctly reflect the convention's articles on freedom of thought/religion and privacy.

Question_Text: With reference to The Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015, consider the following statements: 1. Any child up to the age of 18 years shall be presumed to be innocent of any criminal intent. 2. No waiver of any of the rights of the child is permissible or valid, whether sought by the child or person acting on behalf of the child. 3. All past records of any child under the Juvenile Justice system should be erased without exception. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
Brief_Explanation: Statement 1 is incorrect (children 16-18 can be tried as adults for heinous crimes). Statement 3 is incorrect (records of 16-18 year olds tried as adults are not automatically erased). Statement 2 is a fundamental principle of the Act.

Question_Text: The consistency with which a test measures whatever it measures is best stated as its
Brief_Explanation: Reliability strictly refers to the consistency, stability, and repeatability of test scores over time and across test items.

Question_Text: Which of the following factors are the characteristics of Standardized Achievement test? 1. Reliability 2. Validity 3. Norm Select the correct answer using the code given below:
Brief_Explanation: A standardized test is systematically designed and refined to possess high reliability and validity, and it includes established norms to compare individual performance against a larger group.

Question_Text: In the context of role of objectives in Educational Evaluation, which one of the following illustrative statements of objectives does not fall under Affective Domain?
Option_A: The pupil appreciates a given piece of literature
Option_B: The pupil expresses ideas in writing with good speed and with correct punctuation
Option_D: The pupil develops an interest in reading autobiographies of scientists
Brief_Explanation: Option B describes a physical writing skill paired with cognitive grammatical knowledge, placing it more in the psychomotor/cognitive domains rather than the affective (emotional/attitudinal) domain.

Question_Text: With reference to the factors influencing the reliability of a test, consider the following statements : 1. The more heterogeneous the group, the lesser is the reliability. 2. Adding equivalent items makes a test more reliable, while deleting them makes it less reliable. 3. Too easy or too difficult tests for a group will tend to be less reliable. Which of the statements given above are correct ?
Brief_Explanation: Statement 1 is incorrect because greater group heterogeneity generally increases true score variance, which increases the reliability coefficient. Statements 2 and 3 are standard psychometric principles.

Question_Text: In the context of educational measurement, consider the following statements: 1. Items of the same difficulty level do not always discriminate between students of different achievement levels. 2. If the difficulty level is exactly 0.50, then the discrimination index has its maximum range. Which of the statements given above is/are correct ?
Brief_Explanation: An item can be moderately difficult but poorly written, failing to discriminate top students from bottom students. Statistically, item variance is maximized when item difficulty (p) is 0.50, allowing the highest possible discrimination power.

Question_Text: Which one of the following test scores can be reported to parents for improving their children's achievement ?
Brief_Explanation: Diagnostic test scores provide actionable insights into specific learning gaps and misconceptions, helping parents and teachers target areas for improvement.

Question_Text: Which one of the following is not a Projective Technique ?
Brief_Explanation: A Situational Test is typically an observational or behavioral assessment, whereas Sentence Completion, Word Association, and Inkblots are classic projective psychological tests.

Question_Text: In which of the following situations are sociometric techniques necessarily being used by students ? 1. When they elect their monitor 2. When they do their homework regularly 3. When they choose sides for a game 4. When they listen to the teacher attentively in classroom teaching Select the correct answer using the code given below :
Brief_Explanation: Sociometric techniques analyze social relationships, peer acceptance, and group dynamics, which are actively exercised when students vote for leaders (monitor) or select peers for teams.

Question_Text: What does the drive namely "Operation Blackboard" as envisaged in the National Policy on Education, 1986 imply?
Option_A: To provide blackboard to all primary schools
Option_B: To provide blackboard to all educational institutions
Option_C: To provide essential facilities to primary schools
Option_D: To provide essential facilities to secondary schools
Brief_Explanation: Operation Blackboard was a centrally sponsored scheme designed to provide a minimum level of essential infrastructure and teaching-learning materials to all primary schools.

Question_Text: The main purpose of measuring aptitude is to assess the
Brief_Explanation: Aptitude tests are specifically designed to evaluate a person's potential to succeed in a particular activity or learn a new skill in the future.

Question_Text: Which one of the following best explains the aim of a holistic and multidisciplinary education?
Option_B: To provide access to higher education
Option_C: To increase gross enrolment ratio in higher education
Option_D: To provide opportunity to the children belonging to marginalized sections
Brief_Explanation: Holistic and multidisciplinary education emphasizes integrating intellectual, aesthetic, social, physical, and emotional capacities to develop complete, well-rounded individuals.

Question_Text: Which of the following best defines the concept of Continuous and Comprehensive Evaluation (CCE)?
Option_A: Evaluation of learner performance in cognitive and non-cognitive aspects throughout the teaching-learning process
Option_B: Evaluation of performance by teachers, students and parents
Option_C: Evaluation of learner performance with the help of periodic tests by the teachers
Option_D: Evaluation of learner performance with the help of structured tools at regular intervals
Brief_Explanation: CCE focuses on regular assessments covering both scholastic (cognitive) and co-scholastic (non-cognitive) developmental aspects continuously throughout the academic year.

Question_Text: Consider the following statements: Statement-I: A sound assessment system incorporates both cognitive and non-cognitive aspects of education spread over the total span of instructional time. Statement-II: Learner assessment should be holistic. Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
Option_A: Both the Statements I and II are correct and Statement-II is the correct explanation of Statement-I.
Option_B: Both the Statements I and II are correct, but Statement-II is not the correct explanation of Statement-I.
Option_C: Statement-I is correct, but Statement-II is incorrect.
Option_D: Statement-I is incorrect, but Statement-II is correct.
Brief_Explanation: Statement-II (the principle of holistic assessment) serves as the foundational rationale for Statement-I (the design of a sound system encompassing cognitive and non-cognitive domains).

Question_Text: Consider the following statements: Statement-I: Each individual score contributes to the calculation of "Mean" of scores. Statement-II: "Mean" is a measure of Central Tendency. Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
Option_A: Both the Statements I and II are correct and Statement-II is the correct explanation of Statement-I.
Option_B: Both the Statements I and II are correct, but Statement-II is not the correct explanation of Statement-I.
Option_C: Statement-I is correct, but Statement-II is incorrect.
Option_D: Statement-I is incorrect, but Statement-II is correct.
Brief_Explanation: Both statements are factually true. However, the fact that the mean is a measure of central tendency (Statement II) is not the mathematical reason why every score is included in its calculation (Statement I).

Question_Text: The median and standard deviation of a distribution are 25 and 2.5 respectively. If each item in the distribution is increased by 10, then how are median and standard deviation affected?
Option_A: Median becomes 35, but standard deviation remains unchanged
Option_B: Both median and standard deviation remain unchanged
Option_C: Median becomes 35, but standard deviation becomes 12.5
Option_D: Median remains unchanged, but standard deviation becomes 12.5
Brief_Explanation: Adding a constant to every data point shifts the entire distribution, changing position measures like the median (25+10=35), but it does not change the spread/dispersion, so the standard deviation remains 2.5.

Question_Text: Consider the following statements: 1. Items with difficulty level 0 (zero) have discrimination index 0 (zero). 2. Items with difficulty level 1 (one) have discrimination index 1 (one). Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
Brief_Explanation: If difficulty is 0 (nobody gets it right) or 1 (everyone gets it right), the item fails to differentiate between high and low scorers, so the discrimination index is 0 in both cases. Thus, only statement 1 is correct.

Question_Text: In which of the following cases is median preferred to mean? 1. When distribution of data is skewed 2. When one is dealing with ordinal data 3. When data distribution is continuous 4. When data is normally distributed Select the correct answer using the code given below:
Brief_Explanation: The median is robust against extreme outliers (making it preferred for skewed data) and strictly requires rank ordering (making it suitable for ordinal data). Mean is preferred for normal/continuous data.

Question_Text: What is the z-score of a value of 24, given a mean of 16 and a standard deviation of 4?
Brief_Explanation: The z-score formula is z = (X - Mean) / SD. Here, z = (24 - 16) / 4 = 8 / 4 = 2.0.

Question_Text: Such item of the above difficulty level (obtained in the previous question) would be a good one to place
Option_B: in the midst of a test
Option_C: near the end of a test
Option_D: near the beginning of a test
Brief_Explanation: An item with a difficulty index of 0.75 is relatively easy (75% got it right). Easy items are generally placed at the beginning of a test to help students build confidence and reduce anxiety.

Question_Text: Consider the following in respect of z-score : 1. If the raw score is equal to the mean, then z-score is zero. 2. z-score can be negative. 3. z-score can be a decimal number. Which statements are correct ?
Brief_Explanation: All statements are mathematical facts about z-scores. A score exactly at the mean yields 0; scores below the mean yield negatives; and divisions routinely result in decimals.

Question_Text: Consider the following in respect of skewed distribution : 1. In a positively skewed distribution, the mean falls to the left of the median 2. In a negatively skewed distribution, the mean falls to the right of the median Which of the statements given above is/are correct ?
Brief_Explanation: Both statements are reversed. In a positively skewed (right-skewed) distribution, the long tail pulls the mean to the RIGHT of the median. In a negatively skewed distribution, it pulls it to the LEFT.

Question_Text: The mean of four numbers is 17.5. Out of them the mean of the smaller three numbers is 15. If the range of the data is 15, what is the mean of the larger three numbers?
Brief_Explanation: Sum of all 4 = 17.5*4 = 70. Sum of smaller 3 = 15*3 = 45. Largest number = 70-45=25. Range=15, so smallest = 25-15=10. The 4 numbers sum to 70; excluding the smallest (10), the larger 3 sum to 60. Mean of larger 3 = 60/3 = 20.

Question_Text: Consider the following pairs : Instance - Measurement Scale. 1. Weight in kilograms that a student can lift - Ratio Scale. 2. Number assigned consecutively to students as they complete a test comprising 50 items - Ordinal Scale. Which of the above pairs is/are correctly matched ?
Brief_Explanation: Weight has a true zero (absolute absence), making it a Ratio scale. Consecutive finishing order represents rank without necessarily equal intervals between them, making it an Ordinal scale.

Question_Text: Consider the following pairs : Instance - Measurement Scale. 1. Number of items a student answers correctly in a test comprising 20 items - Ratio Scale. 2. Number assigned to different groups of students each of which solved a certain problem by a different method - Nominal Scale. Which of the above pairs is/are correctly matched ?
Brief_Explanation: A count of correct items has a true zero, making it a Ratio scale. Group classification numbers act solely as arbitrary labels, characteristic of a Nominal scale.

Question_Text: Consider the following statements : 1. A test for recruitment to a post should have high predictive validity. 2. Predictive validity underlines the suitability of candidates to be selected for a training. Which of the statements given above is/are correct ?
Brief_Explanation: Predictive validity measures how well a test forecasts future performance or success, which is the primary goal of recruitment and training selection assessments. Both statements are accurate.

Question_Text: The reliability coefficient of a test is 0.64. What does it indicate?
Option_A: The test measures true ability to the extent of 32%
Option_B: The test measures true ability to the extent of 40%
Option_C: The test measures true ability to the extent of 64%
Option_D: The test measures true ability to the extent of 80%
Brief_Explanation: The reliability coefficient mathematically represents the proportion of true score variance to total observed variance. A coefficient of 0.64 indicates 64% of the variance is true ability.

Question_Text: The mean of set of observations that follow normal distribution is 13.5 and standard deviation is 2.5. What does it indicate ?
Option_A: About 50% of observations fall within 11 and 16
Option_B: About 68% of observations fall within 11 and 16
Option_C: About 95% of observations fall within 11 and 16
Option_D: About 99% of observations fall within 8.5 and 18.5
Brief_Explanation: The range 11 to 16 is calculated by Mean - 1 SD (13.5-2.5=11) to Mean + 1 SD (13.5+2.5=16). In a normal distribution, approximately 68.26% of data falls within ±1 SD of the mean.

Question_Text: In the context of test analysis, consider the following statements : 1. In the Central Tendency of marks obtained by a group, if the values of median and mode are found to be low, then these indices indicate that the test is very hard. 2. If the spread of marks is large and the reliability is low, then standard error is also low. Which of the statements given above is/are correct ?
Brief_Explanation: Statement 1 is true because low central tendency values reflect a positively skewed distribution, typical of a hard test. Statement 2 is false; standard error increases when SD is large and reliability is low.

Question_Text: Consider the following statements : Statement-I: An individual with IQ (Intelligence Quotient) 120 is twice as capable and intelligent as an individual with IQ 60. Statement-II: IQ gives a direct proportional comparison. Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
Option_A: Both the Statements I and II are correct and Statement-II is the correct explanation of Statement-I.
Option_B: Both the Statements I and II are correct, but Statement-II is not the correct explanation of Statement-I.
Option_C: Statement-I is correct, but Statement-II is incorrect.
Option_D: Both the Statements I and II are incorrect.
Brief_Explanation: IQ scores are measured on an interval scale, not a ratio scale, meaning they lack an absolute zero point. Therefore, one cannot mathematically claim that an IQ of 120 is "twice as intelligent" as 60. Both statements are false.

Question_Text: In a group of 100 school children, the reliability coefficient of an achievement test is 0.6. What will be the effect upon test reliability (i.e., reliability coefficient) if the test length is doubled? (Use Spearman-Brown Prophecy formula)
Brief_Explanation: Using the Spearman-Brown formula: r_new = (n * r) / (1 + (n-1)*r). Here n=2 (doubled). r_new = (2 * 0.6) / (1 + (2-1)*0.6) = 1.2 / 1.6 = 0.75.

Question_Text: An educational achievement test has reliability coefficient 0.50. How much should we increase test length to ensure a reliability coefficient of 0.75? (Use Spearman-Brown Prophecy formula)
Brief_Explanation: Let n be the multiplier. 0.75 = (n * 0.5) / (1 + (n-1)*0.5). Simplifying: 0.75 = 0.5n / (0.5 + 0.5n). 0.375 + 0.375n = 0.5n => 0.125n = 0.375 => n = 3. The test must be 3 times as long.

Question_Text: What is the standard deviation of the data 15, 12, 6, 14, 18?
Brief_Explanation: Mean = (15+12+6+14+18)/5 = 13. Deviations: 2, -1, -7, 1, 5. Squared deviations: 4, 1, 49, 1, 25. Variance = Sum of squares / n = 80 / 5 = 16. Standard deviation = square root of 16 = 4.

Question_Text: When variables are measured on nominal scale, the best measure of Central Tendency is
Brief_Explanation: Nominal data represents distinct, unranked categories. Mean and median require numerical values or ordering, leaving the mode (the most frequently occurring category) as the only appropriate measure.

Question_Text: The mean and standard deviation of marks obtained by students of four sections A, B, C, D (each comprising 40 students) of a class are given below: Section A (Mean:30, SD:6), Section B (Mean:40, SD:12), Section C (Mean:36, SD:9), Section D (Mean:25, SD:8). Which one of the four sections shows the lowest variability in marks?
Brief_Explanation: Variability relative to the mean is measured by the Coefficient of Variation (CV) = (SD/Mean)*100. A: 20%, B: 30%, C: 25%, D: 32%. Section A has the lowest CV, indicating the lowest relative variability.

Question_Text: As per the National Education Policy, 2020, the Government of India would set up a "Gender Inclusion Fund". This fund is meant for
Brief_Explanation: NEP 2020 explicitly designates the 'Gender Inclusion Fund' to build capacity for providing equitable quality education for all girls as well as transgender students.

Question_Text: Consider the following with reference to India : 1. Agriculture and allied sectors contribute maximum to Gross Domestic Product. 2. Services sector is treated as a component of Primary sector of economy. Which of the statements given above is/are correct ?
Brief_Explanation: Statement 1 is incorrect as the Services sector contributes the maximum to India's GDP. Statement 2 is incorrect because the Services sector is classified as the Tertiary sector, not Primary.

Question_Text: A person who bribes a public servant for improper performance of a public duty, can be punished with imprisonment, fine, or both under the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988. What is the maximum period for which a person can be imprisoned ?
Brief_Explanation: Under Section 8 of the amended Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988, the offence of bribing a public servant carries a penalty of imprisonment for a term which may extend up to seven years.

Question_Text: Which of the following statements are correct in relation to the Right to Information Act, 2005 ? 1. The term "information" includes samples, models and data held in electronic form. 2. The term "record" includes reproduction of images embodied in microfilms. 3. The right to information does not extend to inspection of work, documents and records. Select the correct answer using the code given below:
Brief_Explanation: Statements 1 and 2 align with the statutory definitions in the RTI Act. Statement 3 is false because the Act explicitly defines the "right to information" to include the right to inspect work, documents, and records.

Question_Text: Within how many days of receiving the decision of a Central Public Information Officer, can an aggrieved person file the first appeal?
Brief_Explanation: Section 19 of the RTI Act, 2005 stipulates that a first appeal must be filed within 30 days from the receipt of the decision of the Public Information Officer.

Question_Text: Which of the following statements is/are correct in relation to the Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act, 2009 ? 1. A child has the right to seek transfer from one school to another except some specified schools, for completing his/her elementary education. 2. The Central and the State Governments shall have concurrent responsibility for providing funds for carrying out provisions of the Act. Select the correct answer using the code given below:
Brief_Explanation: Section 5 of the RTE Act grants the right to transfer, while Section 7 mandates that the Central and State Governments share concurrent financial and other responsibilities to execute the Act. Both statements are accurate.

Question_Text: With reference to the Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act, 2009, which of the following are the duties of appropriate Government? 1. Provide infrastructure including school building, teaching staff and learning equipment. 2. Ensure timely prescribing of curriculum and courses of study for elementary education. 3. Provide training facility for teachers. Select the correct answer using the code given below :
Brief_Explanation: All three points correspond accurately to the duties laid down in Section 8 of the RTE Act, detailing the appropriate government's responsibility to provide infrastructure, curriculum, and teacher training.

Question_Text: Which of the following categories of information is/are exempted from disclosure under the Right to Information Act, 2005 ? 1. Information, disclosure of which would prejudicially affect the scientific or economic interests of the State. 2. Information available to a person in his fiduciary relationship, unless the competent authority is satisfied that the larger public interest warrants the disclosure of such information. Select the correct answer using the code given below:
Brief_Explanation: Both categories are explicitly listed as exemptions under Section 8(1) of the Right to Information Act, 2005.

Question_Text: Which of the following conditions must be satisfied for admission of a Question in the Lok Sabha? 1. It shall not exceed 150 words. 2. It shall not raise larger issues of policy. 3. It shall not go into minor details of administration and day-to-day working of the Government. Select the correct answer using the code given below :
Brief_Explanation: According to the Rules of Procedure and Conduct of Business in Lok Sabha, all three conditions listed limit the scope and format of parliamentary questions to ensure they remain precise and relevant.

Question_Text: What is the minimum imprisonment prescribed in the Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013 ?
Option_D: No imprisonment is prescribed in the Act
Brief_Explanation: The POSH Act itself prescribes disciplinary actions (like deduction from salary) based on service rules. It does not contain a specific imprisonment provision internally, relying instead on IPC provisions for criminal prosecution.

Question_Text: Which one of the following officers is the Chief Accounting Authority in a Central Government Ministry ?
Brief_Explanation: Under the Government of India's financialsystem, the Secretary of the respective Ministry/Department is designated as the Chief Accounting Authority.

Question_Text: Under the Right to Information Act, 2005, if the information sought for concerns the life or liberty of a person, within which time period after the receipt of the request shall the information be supplied ?
Brief_Explanation: Section 7(1) of the RTI Act strictly mandates that if the requested information concerns the life or liberty of a person, it must be provided within forty-eight (48) hours of the receipt of the request.
